objective: Build a simple responsive React Todo app that supports adding, deleting, and completing tasks, persists tasks in localStorage, includes unit tests, and builds successfully with npm run build.
assumptions: Inspect the existing project before choosing tooling; preserve compatible dependencies and conventions.
If no application exists, use React with Vite and JavaScript.
Tasks contain a stable unique id, task text, and a completed boolean.
Completion can be toggled on and off; duplicate task text is allowed.
No backend, authentication, editing, filtering, or cross-tab synchronization is required.
requirements: Render a task-entry form and a list of existing tasks.
Add a task through form submission, supporting both the Add button and Enter key.
Trim task text and reject empty or whitespace-only submissions.
Delete an individual task using its id.
Toggle an individual task's completed state and visually distinguish completed tasks.
Load saved tasks on startup and persist every successful add, delete, or completion change to localStorage.
Keep the application usable if stored data is malformed or localStorage is unavailable.
Provide a basic responsive layout with labeled controls, keyboard accessibility, visible focus states, and readable task text.
Include automated unit and component tests for task behavior and persistence.
Provide working npm test and npm run build scripts.
architecture: Use the existing React toolchain if suitable; otherwise initialize a minimal Vite React application.
src/App.jsx: own task state, initialize it lazily from storage, implement task actions with functional state updates, and compose the interface.
src/components/TaskForm.jsx: manage draft text, validate submissions, call the add callback, and clear the input after a successful addition.
src/components/TaskList.jsx: render the empty state or semantic task list with completion checkboxes and delete buttons.
src/storage.js: define one versioned storage key and guarded load/save functions; validate stored task records.
src/styles.css: provide a centered fluid layout, wrapping task text, responsive form controls, completion styling, and focus styles.
src/storage.test.js and src/App.test.jsx: cover storage utilities and user-visible task behavior using Vitest, React Testing Library, user-event, and jsdom, or equivalent existing tooling.
Keep state local to React; do not add routing, a global state library, or a backend.
implementation_steps: Inspect package.json, source files, repository instructions, and existing tests; identify the smallest compatible changes needed.
Configure React entry points and test tooling only where absent; ensure npm test runs once and npm run build creates a production bundle.

Define the task model and storage key. Implement guarded parsing and validation: accept only arrays of records with unique nonempty string ids, nonempty string text, and boolean completed values; discard invalid records and duplicate ids.
Implement lazy state initialization from storage so saved tasks are loaded before persistence runs. Treat missing, malformed, or non-array data as an empty list.
Implement add, delete, and completion actions using stable ids and immutable functional updates. Generate ids with a browser-supported unique-id mechanism.
Implement the accessible task form, semantic task list, completion checkboxes, task-specific delete labels, and empty-state message.
Persist task state changes through the storage utility. Catch write failures and display a concise nonblocking message that changes may not survive a reload.
Add minimal responsive styles, including safe wrapping for long task text and controls that remain usable on narrow screens.
Write isolated storage unit tests and component tests covering the specified behavior and failure cases.
Run the complete test suite and npm run build, resolve failures, and manually check the production preview on mobile and desktop widths.
edge_cases: Empty or whitespace-only input does not create a task or write a new task record.
Duplicate task text remains independently completable and deletable because actions use ids.
Long text and unbroken strings wrap without horizontal page overflow.
Deleting the final task restores the empty state and persists an empty array.
Missing storage, invalid JSON, unexpected top-level types, invalid records, and duplicate stored ids are handled without crashing.
Storage read or write exceptions leave in-memory task actions usable; write failures produce a nonblocking persistence warning.
Rapid consecutive actions do not lose updates through stale state.
React development Strict Mode does not overwrite saved tasks with an initial empty state.
Task text containing HTML is rendered as plain text.
acceptance_criteria: A user can add a trimmed nonempty task with either Enter or the Add button, and the input clears afterward.
A user can complete and uncomplete a task, with the checkbox state and visual styling reflecting its status.
Deleting a task removes only the selected task, including when multiple tasks have identical text.
After reloading, task text, order, deletions, and completed states match the last successfully persisted state.
Invalid stored data and storage exceptions do not crash the application.
The interface has no horizontal overflow at 320px, 768px, and 1280px viewport widths, including with long task text.
All primary actions work with the keyboard and have accessible names.
Automated tests cover task actions, validation, persistence restoration, persistence updates, and storage failures.
npm test exits successfully without entering watch mode.
npm run build exits successfully and the production preview renders the app.
verification_plan: Unit-test loading valid tasks, missing data, malformed JSON, non-array data, invalid records, duplicate ids, and storage read exceptions.
Unit-test serialization of task arrays, including an empty array, and graceful handling of storage write exceptions.
Component-test adding tasks through both submission methods, trimming text, rejecting blank input, and clearing the input after success.
Component-test completion toggling, deleting individual tasks with duplicate text, and displaying the empty state after the final deletion.
Prepopulate localStorage before rendering and verify initial restoration is not overwritten; perform actions, unmount, and remount to verify persisted state.
Mock storage write failure and verify that task actions still work and a persistence warning appears.
Reset localStorage and restore mocks between tests; query controls by accessible role and name rather than implementation details.
Run npm test and npm run build and record their results.
Inspect the production preview at the specified viewport widths; verify long-text wrapping, keyboard navigation, focus visibility, and real-browser reload persistence.
risks: The existing project structure is unknown; inspect it before introducing or replacing build and test tooling.
localStorage can be blocked, full, or cleared by the browser, so persistence cannot be guaranteed when storage fails.
Multiple open tabs can overwrite each other's saved state; cross-tab synchronization is outside the requested scope.
DOM-based tests do not validate actual responsive layout, so browser verification remains necessary.
